title: Channel surge: joint GTM & opportunity triage with Altair Dynamics
summary: Partner-led GTM plan to accelerate a large account opportunity at Altair Dynamics. Primary blockers: procurement timeline, SOC2 evidence, and on-prem encryption key management. Agreed pilot scope: dedicated capacity POC for 6 weeks, performance benchmark, joint reference deck. Next steps include sending a one-pager, arranging a CISO sync, and scheduling an in-region perf run.
action_items: Maya: send joint solution one-pager and partner pricing matrix by 2027-01-03
Roberto: draft POC runbook and benchmark scripts by 2027-01-05
Lena: intro to CloudLattice channel lead and confirm reseller SKU by 2026-12-30
Altair/Samir: share existing latency & throughput baselines by 2027-01-04
Jordan: share procurement template / expected timeline by 2027-01-07
next_steps: Schedule CISO security review (Lena to coordinate)
Kick off Dedicated POC week-of Jan 9th
Joint exec intro email to Altair VP of Eng and Redwood GM
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-28 09:30 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Roberto Vega (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood Partnerships), Samir Patel (Altair Head of Platform), Elena Ruiz (Altair CTO), Jordan Kim (Altair Procurement)

Topics covered: partner joint GTM, POC scoping, security/QoS, pricing conversation, next steps

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy holidays and we'll try to keep this tight, we put together a quick agenda around the Altair opportunity and how Lena and our channel partner can accelerate the close
[01:05] Samir: thanks Maya, appreciate it, quick context — Altair's been evaluating embeddable inference for product search and recommendations, we want on-prem or VPC with strict KMS controls
[02:20] Elena: and to add, our core ask is sub-200ms tail latency for 512-token queries, 24/7 availability, and we need audit logs retained for 1 year
[03:12] Roberto: understood, good to call that out. Redwood Dedicated supports VPC/private control plane, KMS integrations, and long retention — we'll outline specifics but that aligns
[04:01] Jordan: procurement here — timelinewise we have year-end blackout then coming back first week of Jan to issue PO, but we need reseller terms and an EULA review beforehand
[05:15] Lena: on the partner side, CloudLattice is prepared to resell and manage invoicing — I'll confirm their reseller SKU and margin. we can also co-sell a joint discount for pilot customers
[06:30] Maya: perfect. high level proposal — 6 week Dedicated POC, joint-run perf benchmarks, weekly check-ins. Roberto will own runbook and scripts, Lena will own partner billing path, and we'll loop in Redwood security docs
[07:53] Samir: what does the POC look like operationally? we don't want a long lift, must be minimally invasive
[09:00] Roberto: pragmatic approach — we'll provide a Dedicated instance in a customer-dedicated VPC, set up model variant with quantized profile, and run a synthetic workload that matches your query distribution. we keep KV cache warm for realistic latencies
[10:28] Elena: you said quantized profile — any quality delta risk? we can't drop relevance for recommendations
[11:35] Roberto: great question. we suggest a 16-bit to 8-bit quantization profile validated against your eval set. we always run quality regression checks; if delta > X% we adjust. i'll note that in the runbook
[12:40] Maya: also worth noting our Optimize toolkit can suggest batching/caching parameters by analyzing real traffic — helps lower cost in production post-POC
[13:22] Jordan: procurement is going to need SOC 2 and ISO attestation, plus network diagrams for the VPC setup
[14:10] Lena: i can send CloudLattice's compliance interface doc; Redwood can share SOC2 report and network architecture. we'll put those in a shared folder
[15:45] Samir: re: encryption — must support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) on-prem or cloud KMS. cannot have operator access to keys
[16:38] Roberto: we support KMS integrations; for Private deployments we can configure HSM-backed keywrap and provide role-based access. i'll add the KMS config snippet to the runbook
[17:52] Elena: any known issues with KV cache persistence across restarts? our traffic spikes can cause pod evictions
[19:05] Roberto: we have continuous batching and KV cache eviction policies; for Dedicated capacity we'll pin nodes and can configure cache hot-standby. there might be some warm-up traffic but we'll script ramp tests
[20:40] Maya: pricing question — is there a partner-discounted pilot rate? Altair would like to avoid full list pricing for a POC
[21:30] Lena: yes we typically offer a pilot carveout through our reseller agreements, usually 50% off list for the first 6 weeks with commitment to enterprise contract if successful
[22:10] Jordan: procurement will expect formal quote and reseller invoice template — can that be provided before Jan 4th?
[23:00] Maya: we can produce a quote and the reseller invoice template — Lena will confirm SKUs and finalize numbers by 12/30, we aim to send that week
[24:25] Samir: another blocker — our security team will want to talk to Redwood security lead. can we have a short technical CISO-level call?
[25:10] Maya: absolutely, we suggest a 30-minute CISO sync to go over SOC2, key management, network isolation. Lena can coordinate dates
[26:55] Elena: about SLAs — we need clarity on SLOs for latency and availability and a rollback strategy if model quality regresses after a rollout
[28:05] Roberto: SLOs can be contractually defined; we also support automatic fallback to a smaller model variant or routing to a hosted fallback. we'll include rollback playbook and tracing hooks in the docs
[29:40] Samir: who will own runtime monitoring during the POC? we need token-level cost, latency breakdown, and per-route error traces
[30:30] Maya: Redwood Console provides token-level breakdowns and per-route dashboards. Roberto can show a short demo during the POC kickoff; also we can grant Altair read-only access to the console for the trial
[31:50] Jordan: any data exfiltration concerns with logs? legal will want to ensure logs are stored in our controlled bucket with limited retention
[33:02] Roberto: we can push logs to your S3/GCS bucket in your account and set lifecycle policies. we also support filtering PII at ingestion if needed
[34:20] Elena: can we map this to our internal runbook? we have an internal escalation tree, need to ensure contact points align
[35:05] Maya: we'll align on contact matrix and sev escalation. action owner noted — send a contact template
[36:25] Lena: on go-to-market — team suggested a joint field exec briefing to present the solution to Altair execs, post-POC results, and co-sell motion for a larger roll-out
[37:40] Samir: that would be good, but timing matters — we prefer the exec briefing after perf benchmarks and a successful security review
[38:55] Roberto: for benchmark metrics we'll collect p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, tokens/sec, and quality metrics (MRR or MRR@K depending on your eval). need to confirm the evaluation dataset
[40:03] Samir: i'll share a sanitized eval set and production latency baselines by Jan 4th
[41:18] Maya: great, and on references — CloudLattice can bring a similar customer reference that used our Dedicated setup for recommendation workloads
[42:05] Lena: i'll check with field ops and try to get a reference call queued if helpful
[43:30] Jordan: procurement question — will CloudLattice be on the invoice or Redwood? we prefer a single reseller invoice
[44:12] Lena: CloudLattice will resell and invoice Altair; Redwood will be on the SOW as technology provider. we'll ensure reseller terms are included
[45:25] Elena: is there any IP concern with model artifacts? some of our embeddings are proprietary, we need guarantees they won't be used outside our tenancy
[46:40] Roberto: isolation model — dedicated tenancy, no model sharing, and contractual language around IP. we'll provide a data handling addendum
[47:50] Samir: timeline recap — if POC kicks week of Jan 9, 6 weeks runs to mid-Feb, then exec briefing late Feb, procurement sign late Feb/Mar potentially
[48:35] Maya: sounds realistic. Jordan, does that map to your procurement window?
[49:05] Jordan: yes that should work, assuming we get the reseller quote and SOW early Jan. otherwise it could slip a cycle
[50:28] Maya: ok finalize owners: Maya to send one-pager and pricing matrix, Roberto to deliver runbook and benchmark scripts, Lena to confirm reseller SKU and set up invoicing path, Altair to share baselines and eval set, Jordan to push procurement timeline and template
[51:50] Elena: quick note — we will want a copy of rollback playbook and test of failover during the POC
[52:45] Roberto: we'll include automated failover tests in the runbook and schedule a failover rehearsal mid-POC
[54:10] Maya: any other concerns?
[54:55] Samir: none from me, just want assurance on KMS and SOC2 docs
[55:20] Jordan: i'll wait for the quote, then move to internal legal review
[56:10] Maya: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the docs and next steps by the dates we discussed. happy holidays and we'll reconvene in January

Meeting end

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had some proper noun errors (CloudLattice sometimes mis-transcribed as "Cloud Lattice" or "Cloud Atlas"), occasional speaker mis-attribution. Intentionally kept some disfluencies and pauses to mirror raw transcription.
